fields.lessonRecap: The Cavite Mutiny was a military uprising on 20 January 1872; the later execution was a separate event. GOMBURZA remembers the three priests; reform advocacy alone does not prove involvement in the mutiny. Distinguish the authorities' accusation from evidence of an action; accusation or punishment alone does not prove involvement. The 20 January mutiny preceded the 17 February execution at Bagumbayan in 1872. Rizal's dedication records remembrance and concern about injustice; it does not prove eyewitness knowledge or a single nationwide response.

fields.title: Cavite and GOMBURZA - Mission Quiz
fields.description: Five questions covering the same topics on every attempt. Pass with at least three correct.

fields.title: Locate the Cavite Event
fields.content:
Our new case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. The NHCP execution-site marker links the later accusation against three priests with this January event.

Keep two places separate: Cavite is linked with the uprising; Bagumbayan in Manila is linked with the later execution. Related events in the same year are not necessarily the same event. This introductory timeline does not settle every disagreement about the causes or extent of the uprising.

Your museum task is to locate the event accurately. We study what happened without acting as fighters.

fields.title: Meet the Three Priests
fields.content:
GOMBURZA combines parts of three surnames: Gomes, Burgos and Zamora. Mariano Gomes, Jose Burgos and Jacinto Zamora were three Filipino priests. Some historical writing uses Gomez for Gomes; in this lesson these spellings refer to the same priest.

The NHCP connects their memory with secularization and equal rights. Recall the previous mission: secularization concerns parish administration by secular clergy. Supporting reform does not by itself establish that someone organized a military uprising.

Keep the people card separate from the event card. The combined name remembers three people, not every participant in the Cavite Mutiny.

fields.title: Read the Accusation Carefully
fields.content:
After the uprising, colonial authorities accused the priests of involvement. The NHCP marker describes their involvement as alleged. Alleged means claimed, rather than proven merely by saying it. The National Museum describes suspected treason: a charge of acting against the government to which a person owes allegiance.

A caption should distinguish the accusation from proof. A serious punishment does not by itself prove that an accusation was true. Our classroom cards cannot replace examination of historical records.

Repair this fictional label: "They were accused, so they must have organized the mutiny." An accusation and a proven action are different. You are not asked to decide guilt from three short clues.

fields.title: Place the Loss on the Timeline
fields.content:
The three priests were executed at Bagumbayan in Manila on 17 February 1872. Executed means put to death under a government sentence. This was a serious loss of human life. We remember it respectfully, without showing or acting out how it happened.

The January uprising came first; the February execution followed. Both belong to 1872, but they happened on different days and in different places. Modern memorials remember this loss.

The timeline helps explain the sequence. It is not a countdown or a battle. Your task is to explain what happened first and what followed, while keeping a claim of involvement separate from proof.

fields.title: Build a Remembrance Case Board
fields.content:
Jose Rizal dedicated his second novel, El Filibusterismo, to the memory of the priests. In the dedication he questioned the accusation. This gives evidence of his response, not every Filipino's opinion.

The NHCP also records remembrance within the Katipunan. These responses connect the case with wider concerns for justice and the country. They do not mean one event alone caused every later movement, or that everyone responded alike.

Build a modern case board. Connect an event, a claim and a later response with the kind of information each provides. Then explain why a dedication is evidence of remembrance, not proof that its writer witnessed the uprising.

fields.title: Explain the Whole Case
fields.content:
Your case has three parts. Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication.

The sequence connects events without confusing them. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof. Later remembrance helps explain why the case remained important in concerns about justice and the country.

Complete this report frame silently or with a trusted adult: "The event was ___. The accusation was ___. A later response was ___. It shows ___, but does not prove ___." The quiz checks five lesson topics. If one is difficult, review its scene before targeted practice.
